title: Emotions, Motivation, Cognitive–Metacognitive Strategies, and Behavior as Predictors of Learning Performance in Blended Learning
reason: Moodle log variables (missing/turned-in activities, partially viewed materials, time spent) are correlated per student with overall grade and with MSLQ motivation and strategy subscales, and enter hierarchical regression on grade.

extraction.n_quote: empirical study in a higher educational course with 137 Mexican students.
extraction.population: undergraduate chemical biology students in a blended applied-computing course, Instituto Politécnico Nacional
extraction.lms_indicators: number of missing (and turned-in) learning activities, partially and fully viewed SCORM materials, time spent in Moodle
extraction.outcome_or_construct: overall course grade; MSLQ motivation and cognitive-metacognitive strategy subscales; SEDS engagement/disaffection

effect_sizes.between: partially viewed materials ↔ overall grade; time spent ↔ overall grade
missing learning activities ↔ MSLQ self-efficacy; partially viewed materials ↔ self-efficacy
missing learning activities ↔ metacognitive self-regulation; partially viewed materials ↔ metacognitive self-regulation

effect_sizes.value: −0.19 (p<.01) in Model 4 with motivation, emotion and strategy predictors, R2 = .693

extraction.notes: In the text file the minus sign is rendered as control character U+0002; quotes keep it verbatim. Time spent unrelated to grade. Missing activities partly define the grade (authors acknowledge). Spent time row shows implausible max < mean (as printed).
